- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > +0.3) and price is trending up, model often under-anticipates continuation; add 3–7% buffer to forecast for next 5–7 periods.  
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment to early forecast values to compensate for lag.  
- If sentiment turns sharply negative mid-forecast horizon, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 2–4 periods to reflect sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates volatility in early days; cap forecast variance within 10% of recent 7-day moving average to avoid overreaction.
